headline: JUNE CPI -0.1% MOM COLLAPSES RATE-HIKE ODDS — GOLD SURGES AS DOLLAR AND YIELDS SINK ON SOFTEST PRINT IN 18 MONTHS
snippet: June CPI came in at approximately -0.1% month-on-month — the first negative monthly print in 18 months, driven by a 10% gasoline price collapse as the US-Iran ceasefire reopened the Strait of Hormuz — pulling the year-over-year rate from May's 4.2% toward approximately 3.9% and crushing September rate-hike odds that had been trading above 60%; gold surged from session lows near $4,001 as the dollar and real yields retreated sharply. Fed Chair Warsh testified 90 minutes after the 8:30 AM ET release and reinforced the soft print's signal by noting that price risks were coming down — a one-two punch that validated gold's safe-haven and inflation-hedge dynamics simultaneously and confirmed mid-July as the seasonal inflection point that historically opens the autumn precious metals rally.

headline: MIATA DRILLS SELA CREEK'S BEST HOLE YET — 30m AT 4.06 g/t AU INCL. 14m AT 8.20 g/t; FOURTH 100+ GRAM-METRE RESULT FROM SURINAME GOLD CORRIDOR (TSXV:MMET)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Miata Metals Corp.
snippet: Miata Metals Corp. (TSXV: MMET) announced July 13 that hole 26DDH-JT-019 at the Jons Trend target on the Sela Creek Gold Project in Suriname returned 30.0 metres at 4.06 g/t gold, including 14.0 metres at 8.20 g/t — the highest-grade intercept the company has ever reported at Sela Creek and the fourth result exceeding 100 gram-metres from the Jons Trend-Big Berg Corridor in the past four months. The hole is a down-dip step-out from previously reported high-grade Jons Trend mineralisation; companion hole 26DDH-BB-013, drilled 150 metres west toward Jons Trend, added 16.5 metres at 2.15 g/t Au — together reinforcing the geological model of a broad, stacked, structurally controlled gold system, with the fully funded 25,000-metre 2026 program now approximately 50% complete and drilling continuing across six targets.

headline: FURY GOLD DRILLS 7.01 g/t OVER 21m — BEST GRADE EVER AT EAU CLAIRE, JAMES BAY; THIRD DRILL RIG MOBILIZED AS HIGH-GRADE SHOOT EXPANDS (TSX:FURY)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Fury Gold Mines Limited
snippet: Fury Gold Mines Limited (TSX: FURY) released July 13 the second batch of assay results from its Phase 2 drill program at the Eau Claire gold project in the Eeyou Istchee Territory, James Bay Region of Northern Quebec — highlight hole 26EC-115 intersected 7.01 g/t gold over 21.0 metres, including 10.27 g/t over 11.0 metres, the highest grade per intercept of comparable true thickness reported at Eau Claire to date. Fury simultaneously mobilized a third diamond drill rig to the project; the accelerated three-rig program — drilling a Phase 2 campaign designed to test both conversion and step-out targets — has now produced its single strongest hole just as the high-grade shoot remains open in multiple directions, validating the capital commitment with the strongest geological signal the project has yet delivered.

headline: COPPER AND ALUMINUM SURGE ON CPI RELIEF — INDUSTRIAL METALS REVERSE IRAN-DRIVEN LOSSES AS RATE-HIKE PREMIUM FADES FROM BASE METALS
snippet: LME copper and aluminum both extended gains July 14 as the June CPI print eased fears of further Federal Reserve rate hikes and improved the outlook for manufacturing demand — copper had been pricing in a rate-hike premium since Iran's Hormuz closure spiked crude oil and stoked inflation fears, and the soft Tuesday print reversed that premium, adding to momentum from fading oil prices and Chinese fund flows into industrial metal stocks ahead of anticipated solid H1 producer earnings. The copper rebound follows a 0.64% drop on July 13 to $13,398/t and is consistent with copper's historical pattern of recovering within one session of a CPI print that eliminates imminent rate-hike risk.

headline: GOLD ROYALTY ADDS REN INTEREST, STERLING AND GRANITE CREEK NEVADA NSRS FOR $800K — ANGLOGOLD AND i-80 GOLD OPERATORS ON BOTH NEW ROYALTIES (NYSE:GROY)
snippet: Gold Royalty Corp. (NYSE: GROY) announced July 13 the acquisition of two additional Nevada royalties from a private seller for combined consideration of US$0.8 million: a 2.0% NSR on AngloGold Ashanti's producing Sterling property south of Gold Royalty's Arthur project, and a 0.5% NSR on i-80 Gold's Granite Creek operation covering the Felix and Blue Bell pits with associated advance minimum royalty payments of $31,500/year — while simultaneously acquiring an additional interest in the REN royalty. The transactions exemplify Gold Royalty's strategy of acquiring producing or near-producing royalty interests from private sellers at below-replacement cost, consolidating Nevada operator coverage as the company heads toward its Q2 2026 results release on August 5.

headline: 'FED IS SPLIT 9 TO 8': FOMC MINUTES REVEAL NEAR-HISTORIC HAWK-DOVE DIVIDE AS JUNE CPI RESOLVES THE RATE STANDOFF FOR GOLD
snippet: GoldSilver.com's market analysis of the June FOMC meeting minutes reveals the most closely divided Fed since before the 2008 financial crisis — nine members prepared to hold rates while eight wanted to raise, a near-unanimous hawkish Committee tilt that explains why gold has corrected approximately 9% from January's $5,405 record to its ~$4,001 July low. The piece argues that this level of institutional ambiguity — where a single data point can flip the outcome — means gold's correction is driven by uncertainty rather than deteriorating fundamentals; a soft CPI print collapses the hike camp and releases months of coiled upside pressure in one session, making July 14 the most binary week for precious metals investors since the April FOMC decision.

headline: GOLD SWOT: DPM METALS Q2 BEATS BY 31% AT VARÈS; TOREX MISSES 10% — MID-JULY SEASONAL LAUNCH WINDOW FOR AUTUMN GOLD RALLY NOW OPEN
snippet: Kitco's weekly Gold SWOT for July 13 highlights DPM Metals' Q2 production beat — output exceeded Canaccord's estimate by 31% as the Varès mine's planned plant shutdown was completed in seven days versus the scheduled 20, with Chelopech GEO rising on higher planned gold and silver grades — while flagging Torex Gold's 10% production miss as the sector's cautionary counterpoint amid Media Luna's lower-grade mine sequencing zone. The broader market context: gold miners are tracking their 12th consecutive quarter of substantial earnings growth at an average AISC of $1,703/oz versus prevailing gold prices, yet the GDX/GDXJ remain at their most oversold relative to fundamentals since the nascent phase of the current bull market — a structural setup the piece argues confirms mid-July as the seasonal launch window for the autumn rally.

headline: TOTAL METALS WRAPS ELECTROLODE WINTER PROGRAM — HORNET ZONE HITS 2.90% ZN, 1.15% CU OVER 7.67m IN ONTARIO CRITICAL METALS VMS DISTRICT (TSXV:TT)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Total Metals Corp.
snippet: Total Metals Corp. (TSXV: TT) released July 13 assay results from 15 of the 25 holes in its completed 8,408-metre 2026 winter program at the Electrolode Critical Metals Project 69 km from Ear Falls, Ontario — the best Hornet Zone intercept returned 2.90% Zn, 1.15% Cu, 13.30 g/t Ag over 7.67 metres including 3.62% Zn, 3.19% Cu, 37.29 g/t Ag over 1.74 metres. The Arrow Zone at Electrolode hosts an existing Inferred Resource of 2.11 million tonnes at 0.66% Cu, 4.74% Zn, 17.92 g/t Ag and 0.66 g/t Au; the Hornet Zone results add a second mineralised zone to the project's footprint in a Red Lake belt more commonly associated with gold, reinforcing Electrolode's position as one of the few active zinc-copper-silver VMS projects in Ontario advancing toward a maiden multi-zone resource estimate.

headline: FIRST TELLURIUM MOBILIZES DEER HORN CREWS — WORLD'S FEW 43-101 TELLURIUM RESOURCES OPENS B.C. POLYMETALLIC SEASON ACROSS 17.5 km² (CSE:FTEL)
source_name: Investing News Network / First Tellurium Corp.
snippet: First Tellurium Corp. (CSE: FTEL) announced July 13 that with its five-year exploration permit approved for commencement of work July 15, the company is mobilizing crews to its Deer Horn polymetallic property in west-central British Columbia — host to one of the world's few NI 43-101 compliant tellurium resources and a 17.5 km² mineral zone encompassing a copper-gold porphyry with surface bornite and a 2.4-kilometre strike length of high-grade gold-silver-tellurium veining. Tellurium, critical for photovoltaic cells, thermoelectric modules, and next-generation semiconductor applications, has no economically viable non-byproduct primary mine supply globally; Deer Horn's position as one of the few primary tellurium resource projects worldwide gives it structural importance at a time when Western critical minerals policy is routing exploration capital into non-standard metals with supply chain dependencies.
